summary: Populate the message store on personal Microsoft (MSA) accounts via per-folder sync; drop the non-existent /me/messages/delta resource; add a sync --folder flag.
reason: The generated sync emitted a dependent resource named "folders" that fetched /me/mailFolders/{id}/messages but wrote the results back into the folders table, leaving the messages table empty. It also listed a "messages-delta" resource pointing at /me/messages/delta, which Microsoft Graph does not implement (message change-tracking exists only per-folder at /me/mailFolders/{id}/messages/delta), so it returned HTTP 400 on every account. On personal Microsoft accounts the global /me/messages collection also returns empty. Net effect: the local message store never populated on MSA, disabling every store-backed feature (since, senders, followup, waiting, digest, stale-unread, quiet, conversations). The fix renames the dependent resource to "messages" (ordered before attachments, which iterates the messages table as its parent), drops the messages-delta resource, and adds --folder to scope a sync to a single mail folder via /me/mailFolders/{folder}/messages.
validated_outcome: Patch-relevant checks pass: go build ./..., go vet, --help, --version, manifest, phase5, transcendence. Three checks (go mod tidy, govulncheck stdlib advisories GO-2026-5039/5037, and a SKILL.md install-section drift) fail identically on the clean upstream baseline and are pre-existing / unrelated to this patch. Live test on a personal MSA mailbox: `sync --folder inbox` stored 10 messages and a full sync stored 129 records across 8 resources with 0 errors — previously the messages-delta resource returned HTTP 400 and the messages table held a single row.
